name: Halverson Synth-Wool Occasion Tuxedo
description:
A single-button tuxedo in a deep charcoal synth-wool blend with a satin-analog lapel that catches light cleanly without looking cheap. Halverson's mid-market tuxedo line is built for the Tier 2-3 customer who attends corporate events, union ceremonies, or the occasional Tier 3 social function and needs to look correctly dressed without spending a month's rent. The jacket features augment-compatible seaming at the shoulders and a discreet port-access panel along the left side, closed with a magnetic seam that lies flush when not in use. The trousers have a single satin-analog stripe down each leg and are cut with enough room in the seat to accommodate minor geneware — standard tail modifications require aftermarket alteration.

It is not a remarkable garment. That is precisely its value. A person wearing this tuxedo registers as appropriately formal and nothing more — no tier signal strong enough to cause friction, no affiliation display to read. For Tier 2 workers attending Tier 3 functions, invisibility is the point.
cultural_context: The default tuxedo of Meridian's working professional class. Rental versions circulate widely through Tier 2 social networks. Owning one rather than renting signals a degree of social ambition. Seen at union investiture ceremonies, corporate welcome events, and Tier 3 weddings.
story_hooks: A character buys this tuxedo specifically for a job interview at a Tier 4 corponation. They are told, gently, that the event is business casual. They wear it anyway.
The augment port panel is a standard feature, but someone has modified theirs to conceal a secondary compartment. Whatever was inside it is gone. The previous rental owner left no other trace.
Two colleagues show up to the same corporate gala in identical Halverson tuxedos. The evening becomes about something other than the event.
